name: THE FUNERAL
materialIdentity: Thad's own plot at the end of Boot Hill's third row, at night under a clear sky full of stars and the moon: the town in black at the grave, the pine coffin on its trestles, the hearse and its mule; after the burial, the hill empty and the grave dug open (errata 99 G, K)
note: Room 31, doc 20: the funeral, reached from Boot Hill once the executor is named (E6). Doc 48 S2 stages it -- the player wanders his own funeral; beat 3 is Hob's 'Good turnout.' on the second LOOK at the grave or at the way back; doc 57 E7's THE COFFIN · USE lies him down and Room 32 begins. When HOB_C1 ends Room 32 hands him back here at night beside the open grave (E8), and T_FUNERAL_DONE is written by his line (errata 99 G).

exits.name: BOOT HILL, BEYOND

LOOK_AT.say: The rest of Boot Hill, rising behind in rows. My new neighbors, keeping a respectful distance.
repeat: Ezra Pike is up there, third row, second from the end. I came a very long way to join him.
From here the markers look like a crowd that came early and sat down.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind through the grass between the rows.
repeat: Nothing. The neighborhood is quiet, as advertised.
A loose board on some marker up the hill, tapping, like somebody keeping time for the service.

transitScene.sceneLine: docs/48-act-turn-beats.md::## S2 · THE FUNERAL (Act III opening) · beat 3

transitScene.say: It is my funeral. I should stay for it.
transitScene.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::## E7 · The coffin · During the funeral

exits.note: Doc 54: the rest of Boot Hill rising behind in rows -- the way back toward it (doc 20). Doc 48 S2 beat 3 plays here if it has not yet ('or on exit toward Boot Hill'); after it, doc 57 E7: 'During the funeral, Room 31's exits are refused.' At night it is the way down (errata 99 G).

props.note: The hearse, and the pine coffin on its trestles in front of it with its lid propped and the name plate on the lid (doc 05, doc 54). One prop: they arrive and leave together. Cut from room-31's composition master by tools/art/room31-cast.py; gone by night (doc 57 E8).

generated.note: GENERATED. Edit the documents or the annotation, never this file.

entrances.note: Up from Boot Hill, at the back of the gathering (doc 48 S2 beat 1: 'Thad at the back').
Out of the grave, at night (doc 57 E8: 'Thad is in Room 31 at night beside the open grave').

LOOK_AT.say: THADDEUS GRUB, it says. Even my death is missing a B.
repeat: The engraver gave the G a flourish he could not afford to give the rest.
It will be on the lid, over my face, for the next few minutes of my life. I'd have liked it spelled right for that.
then: I'd complain, but the plate was free, and so, apparently, was I.

LISTEN_TO.say: Brass. It rings a little flat, which in this town is house style.
repeat: A faint ring when the wind catches the lid. Flat, as noted.
Nothing. Brass keeps its opinions about spelling to itself.

LOOK_AT.say: The undertaker's wax lilies, making their weekly appearance.
repeat: Somebody has wiped the dust off them for the occasion. That is the undertaker's idea of grief, and I find I accept it.
They lean toward the grave, the way everything here eventually does.
then: We are old colleagues by now, the lilies and I.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. They are beyond all that, as previously established.
repeat: A faint tap of wax on wax when the wind finds them.
Nothing. They have outlived everyone they were ever arranged for, and they will outlive me, technically.

LOOK_AT.say: A board, painted while the paint lasted: my name, one date, and HE TUNED.
repeat: THADDEUS GRUBB. Frame supplied the spelling and got it right, once, for a grave I am not going to be in.
The paint has run on the D's. My name is weeping slightly, which is more than I expected of it.
then: As epitaphs in Boot Hill run, that is generous and accurate, which puts it in rare company.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wet paint, drying. My legacy, curing in the night air.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing now. The paint has set. It is official.

LOOK_AT.say: Six feet, measured. I am two inches shorter than the hole, which is the first time this town has given me room.
LOOK_AT.sceneLine: docs/48-act-turn-beats.md::## S2 · THE FUNERAL (Act III opening) · beat 3

LOOK_AT.say: Dug neat, in a good spot, uphill of the seepage — the undertaker does honest work for dishonest occasions. I am oddly touched by the drainage.
repeat: Six feet, measured. I am two inches shorter than the hole, which is the first time this town has given me room.
A plank is laid across it for the pallbearers. It looks like a very short bridge to nowhere in particular.

LISTEN_TO.say: Loose soil trickling back in. The ground, impatient.
repeat: A clod falling from the edge, then another. The ground is in a hurry.
Nothing for a moment. Then the wind across the top of it, a low, open note.

overrides.CLOSE: Not yet. There is a man not in that box counting on the delay.

LOOK_AT.say: Sowerby at grade-two sincerity, which I paid for, delivering me to my reward.
repeat: He is preparing to deliver four words for fifty cents and he is preparing thoroughly.
He has a card in his palm with the adjectives on it and is ticking them off as he goes. I'm getting exactly what I paid for.
then: He keeps almost catching my eye and electing not to.

LISTEN_TO.say: '…a man of music, taken flat…' — he wrote that this morning and is proud of it.
repeat: Nothing yet.
'…a man who came among us, and stayed…' — that one was free, I think. He has thrown it in.

TALK_TO.say: He is mid-adjective. Interrupting would cost us both.
TALK_TO.sceneLine: docs/54-batch-c.md::# ROOM 31 · THE FUNERAL >> ## Overrides · during the service

LOOK_AT.say: At the back, not singing: Hob, hat in hand, watching a funeral he knows to be empty with an expression I cannot price. It takes one to know one, I suppose.
repeat: The night watchman, standing at the back, off his rounds. I have never once seen him stand still.
He has not looked at the coffin once. He has looked at me twice.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing from him. He mourns the way he watches.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing. I have never heard a man be so quiet on purpose.

TALK_TO.say: Not here. Not with the whole town watching me be dead.
TALK_TO.sceneLine: docs/54-batch-c.md::# ROOM 31 · THE FUNERAL >> ## Overrides · before S2 beat 3

LOOK_AT.say: Every man here has taken his hat off. For me.
repeat: Hats of every class, held against every chest. A hat is the only formal clothing most of these men own.
One man is holding two hats. I would like to know whose the other one is, and I am not going to ask at a funeral.
then: On the strength of a notice in the Clarion that misspelled my name.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Nobody fans himself with a hat at a funeral.
repeat: A brim being turned in nervous fingers, round and round.
Nothing. Seven hats, held still.

LOOK_AT.say: The dirt that was in the hole, beside the hole, waiting.
repeat: A shovel stands upright in it, waiting for a volunteer, and nobody is looking at it.
It is exactly the size of the hole. Nothing is ever wasted at the undertaker's.
Loose earth sliding down its side, rehearsing.
Nothing. It is very patient, for dirt.

LOOK_AT.say: Clear, very high and full of stars.
repeat: One cloud, keeping to itself across the moon.
I am going to want to remember this sky in a few minutes. I am trying to look at it properly.
then: It is a beautiful night to be buried, if one has to be.

LISTEN_TO.say: An owl, somewhere up the hill, asking one long question.
repeat: Nothing up there. The sky is not attending.
Wind, high and thin. The last open-air sound for a while.

LOOK_AT.say: My coffin. Pine, with handles and a name plate. I am given to understand I look natural.
repeat: The lid is propped against the trestle, waiting for me, like a coat held out by a valet.
Someone has put a cushion in it. I suspect the undertaker, and I suspect he will charge.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing from inside, which is the least I can do.
repeat: Nothing.
Nothing yet. That changes shortly, and I am trying not to think about it.

USE.say: Not yet. I should stand at my own graveside a moment first. A man only gets the one.
This is the part of the plan where I lie down.

then.speaker: funeral_undertaker
then.line: Lid stays loose. Knock twice when they've gone.

USE.sceneLine: docs/57-puzzle-completion.md::## E7 · The coffin · after S2 beat 3

overrides.OPEN: Ahead of schedule. The lid stays shut; the plan requires my absence and I am contractually elsewhere.
overrides.USE: It is in use. By me. Officially. The paperwork is immaculate.

LOOK_AT.say: Grievance in the hearse harness, wearing black well, as advertised.
repeat: A black ribbon is plaited into her mane. She has allowed this, which is a greater tribute than anything Sowerby will say.
She keeps her head turned a little toward the coffin. I do not think she is fooled.
then: She has attended more funerals than the Reverend and behaves better at them.

LISTEN_TO.say: A slow breath through the nose. Professional composure.
repeat: A hoof shifting once in the soft earth, then still.
Nothing. She is standing at attention, and she means it more than the mourners do.

LOOK_AT.say: A respectable turnout for a man of my brief acquaintance.
repeat: Seven people have come to my funeral. I have been in Consolation less than a month. I do not know what to do with this and I am going to have to get into the box shortly.
One of them is holding his hat over his heart and his other hand over his wallet. He has been to funerals here before.
then: Several are here for the singing. One is here for the will. There is no will.

LISTEN_TO.say: Shuffling, a cough, and somewhere in the middle of it, genuine crying.
repeat: Nothing. Seven people, not talking.
A sniff at the back, and then a nose blown into a sleeve with real feeling.
then: I was not prepared for the crying.

overrides.TALK_TO: A stranger offered me comfort at my own funeral. I said the departed sounded like a fine man, taken too soon. He agreed, with feeling. I'm having a very strange week.

onEnter.note: Doc 57 E8: out of Room 32 and HOB_C1, Thad on the hill at night; his line writes T_FUNERAL_DONE.
say: Out. I have been buried and dug up in one evening, and of the two I preferred the second.

figureLight.note: Errata 109, from the pre-playthrough art audit: the graveside is moonlit, and its whole cast -- Sowerby, the undertaker, the mourners -- was drawn in that cold light, while Thad, drawn in even neutral light for every room, stood among them warm, as if lit by a different lamp. A cool multiply and a little less brightness put him under the same moon. A measurement, not a verdict: Tyler's playthrough decides.
